details.publicNotes:
Vitality energy is the essence of growth and renewal, but not all renewal is healthy for the creatures exposed to it. When a core of vitality energy infests a mass of plant life, it occasionally mutates into an endless growth. As its name suggests, an endless growth expands continuously, and when it finally grows too large to move, it splits into four smaller copies to move to new locations and continue growing. However, this division is far from the creature's only means of propagation. It instinctively seeks to use all other living creatures as fuel to make more of its kind. When its thorny burls injure a creature, it infests their blood with a disease that gradually converts their flesh into another endless growth. It can also eject its own ravenous tumors, which rapidly consume vitality before taking on a life of their own.

Plant and fungal life around an endless growth and its ever-expanding brood of progeny transforms into a blighted forest. Growths and lesions such as burls, cankers, galls, and witch's brooms are commonplace in these lands, along with more unusual mutations. The alchemical and medicinal potential of the rapid mutations that endless growths generate is substantial. Several groups of researchers have decided that it was worth the risk of cultivating their blighted forests deliberately, only to find themselves overrun by the forest's relentlessly hungry denizens.

The Living All

Some misguided forest dwellers worship endless growths as something akin to gods. Believing the growths are a physical manifestation of the intangible force that gives life to all things—a power they name "the Living All"—these wayward souls make living sacrifices to the growths to encourage their spread throughout the Universe. That their gods sometimes find fertile soil in their own flesh seems to make little difference to the devotees of the Living All.

Suggested Monster Parts

Monster Parts 90/200/360 gp

Eligible Refinements weapons (bludgeoning, piercing), armor (heavy), perception item, skill items (Acrobatics, Athletics, Stealth)

Eligible Imbued Properties body, bane, constitution, death, energy resistant (vitality), life, lifeward armor, sensory (low-light vision), strength, tangle shield, throwing, wild, wood

Plants, fungi, and creatures with void healing are immune to Flesh Conversion

Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:25]

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (1 hour)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} (1 hour)

Stage 3 when rolling a recovery check, the creature's degree of success is one degree better (3 hours)

Stage 4 the creature gains fast healing 5 (5 hours)

Stage 5 the creature gains lifesense 60 feet and regeneration 10 (deactivated by void) (1 day)

Stage 6 the creature dies and its body is fully converted into new endless growth.

Requirements The living growth's last action was a successful parasitic tumor Strike that damaged a living creature. The damaged creature isn't @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 4} and doesn't already have an infectious growth attached to it

Effect The parasitic tumor attempts to attach itself to the creature's body (@Check[fortitude|dc:25] negates). If it succeeds, the creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}. This is cumulative with other drained conditions from infectious growth. At the end of each of its turns, a creature with an attached parasitic tumor must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:25] save. On a failure, the value of its drained condition increases by 1. If the value of the drained condition reaches 4, the parasitic tumor then falls off and develops into a new endless growth over the next 24 hours. The affected creature or an adjacent creature can remove the tumor with a successful @Check[medicine|dc:31] check. The tumor automatically falls off if the creature takes void damage or critically succeeds at their Fortitude save to resist the drained condition.
